title: The Truth Behind One Photograph
locale: 山口県公立高校入試型
sentences: Our school newspaper planned a story about a new park, but one photograph caused an argument before publication.
The picture showed a crowded playground and a caption saying, 'The park is always too busy for children.'
Ken wanted to print it immediately because the image looked convincing and several students had shared it online.
Mika asked who had taken the photograph and whether it showed a typical afternoon or a special event with unusual crowds.
We contacted the photographer, who explained that the image was taken during the park's opening celebration last month.
The event had attracted visitors from nearby towns, and the photographer had never claimed that every afternoon looked the same.
We then visited the park on three weekdays and counted children using the playground at four in the afternoon each day.
On Monday we counted twelve, on Tuesday nineteen, and on Wednesday fifteen children near the equipment.
The park manager said the playground could comfortably hold thirty, so none of our three counts showed that it had reached its usual capacity.
However, one parent told us that the entrance path became crowded when students left school together.
We realized that counting playground users alone could miss a different problem near the entrance at certain times.
Mika suggested separate observations of the entrance and a question about how safe families felt when crossing the road beside the park.
Ken agreed that the original caption was too strong, because one crowded celebration could not prove what happened every day.
We decided to publish the photograph with its correct date and event description, not a claim about the park being always crowded.
Beside it, we printed a small table of our three weekday observations and explained the limits of those numbers.
We also included the parent's concern about the crowded entrance and asked readers to share further experiences.
Our teacher checked that the article distinguished what we had actually observed from ideas that still needed more evidence.
The photographer thanked us for correcting the caption because an accurate picture can still create a false impression with the wrong words.
Ken said he would check dates and context before sharing another surprising image with his friends in the future.
I learned that a photograph can tell the truth about one moment, without telling the whole story of a place.
Good reporting means asking what the image leaves out and giving readers enough evidence to think beyond the first impression.
fullTranslation:
学校新聞は新しい公園を紹介する予定でしたが、掲載前に一枚の写真をめぐって議論になりました。
写真には混雑した遊び場が写り、「子どもにはいつも混みすぎる公園」という説明が付いていました。
ケンは写真が説得力を持ち、何人かがネットで共有していたので、すぐ掲載しようと言いました。
ミカは撮影者と、写真が普通の午後なのか特別な行事の日なのかを確かめようとしました。
写真の撮影者に連絡すると、先月の開園記念行事の最中に撮ったものだと分かりました。
行事には町外からも人が集まっており、撮影者は普段も同じ混雑だとは言っていませんでした。
そこで私たちは平日に三回、午後四時に遊び場を利用する子どもの数を調べました。
月曜日は十二人、火曜日は十九人、水曜日は遊具の近くで十五人を数えました。
管理者によれば快適な利用の目安は三十人で、三回の調査ではどの日もそこに達していませんでした。
一方、ある保護者は生徒が一斉に下校すると入口の通路が混むと話しました。
私たちは遊び場の人数だけでは、特定の時間帯に起こる入口付近の問題を見逃すと気づきました。
ミカは入口を別に観察し、公園横の道路を渡るときの安全について家族に尋ねようと提案しました。
ケンは一度のイベント写真では毎日の様子を証明できないと認め、説明を改めることにしました。
写真には正しい撮影日と行事名を付け、「いつも混む」という説明は取りやめました。
写真の横には平日の三回の観察表を載せ、その数字だけでは分からないことも説明しました。
さらに入口の混雑についての保護者の声を載せ、読者にも経験を寄せてもらうことにしました。
先生は記事が観察した事実と、まだ追加の根拠が必要な考えを区別しているか確認しました。
撮影者は正確な写真でも説明が間違えば誤解を生むとして、修正に感謝しました。
ケンは今後、驚く写真を友達に共有する前に撮影日と背景を確かめると言いました。
私は写真がある一瞬の事実を示しても、その場所のすべてを語るわけではないと学びました。
よい記事とは写真に写っていないことも考え、読者が第一印象を越えて判断できる根拠を示すものだと思います。

materials.title: Weekday playground counts at 16:00
materials.note: Crowded photograph was from the previous month's opening celebration, not a typical weekday.

questions.prompt: When had the crowded photograph been taken?
questions.answer: During the park's opening celebration last month.
questions.evidence: We contacted the photographer, who explained that the image was taken during the park's opening celebration last month.
questions.evidenceJp: 写真の撮影者に連絡すると、先月の開園記念行事の最中に撮ったものだと分かりました。
questions.reason: 5文目で先月の開園イベントとある。

questions.prompt: On which surveyed weekday did the class observe the most children?
questions.evidence: On Monday we counted twelve, on Tuesday nineteen, and on Wednesday fifteen children near the equipment.
questions.evidenceJp: 月曜日は十二人、火曜日は十九人、水曜日は遊具の近くで十五人を数えました。

questions.prompt: Why did Ken change his view of the original caption?
questions.answer: One unusual event could not prove the park was always crowded.
questions.evidence: Ken agreed that the original caption was too strong, because one crowded celebration could not prove what happened every day.
questions.evidenceJp: ケンは一度のイベント写真では毎日の様子を証明できないと認め、説明を改めることにしました。
questions.reason: 一回の特別な混雑で毎日を断定できないから。

questions.prompt: Choose the true statement: A Tuesday exceeded thirty; B the playground's comfort guideline was thirty; C all three days had the same count; D the photo was taken on Wednesday.
questions.evidence: The park manager said the playground could comfortably hold thirty, so none of our three counts showed that it had reached its usual capacity.
questions.evidenceJp: 管理者によれば快適な利用の目安は三十人で、三回の調査ではどの日もそこに達していませんでした。
questions.reason: 管理者が目安は30人と述べる。

questions.prompt: Why was studying only playground numbers insufficient?
questions.answer: The entrance might be crowded even if the playground was not.
questions.evidence: We realized that counting playground users alone could miss a different problem near the entrance at certain times.
questions.evidenceJp: 私たちは遊び場の人数だけでは、特定の時間帯に起こる入口付近の問題を見逃すと気づきました。
questions.reason: 入口の別の問題は遊び場の人数から分からない。

questionSetB.prompt: Where would 'This gave readers the real background of the crowded scene.' fit: after sentence 4, 9, 14, or 19?
questionSetB.evidence: We decided to publish the photograph with its correct date and event description, not a claim about the park being always crowded.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 写真には正しい撮影日と行事名を付け、「いつも混む」という説明は取りやめました。
questionSetB.reason: 14文目の正しい撮影日と行事名の説明を受ける。

questionSetB.prompt: Complete: A photo may show one moment without telling the _____ story.
questionSetB.evidence: I learned that a photograph can tell the truth about one moment, without telling the whole story of a place.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 私は写真がある一瞬の事実を示しても、その場所のすべてを語るわけではないと学びました。

questionSetB.prompt: Complete the word: The wrong c______ may give a false impression.
questionSetB.evidence: The photographer thanked us for correcting the caption because an accurate picture can still create a false impression with the wrong words.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 撮影者は正確な写真でも説明が間違えば誤解を生むとして、修正に感謝しました。
questionSetB.reason: 写真説明を示すcaptionが根拠。

questionSetB.prompt: How many more children were observed Tuesday than Monday?
questionSetB.evidence: On Monday we counted twelve, on Tuesday nineteen, and on Wednesday fifteen children near the equipment.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 月曜日は十二人、火曜日は十九人、水曜日は遊具の近くで十五人を数えました。

questionSetB.prompt: Which is the best lesson? A Images need no context; B Captions always tell every fact; C Accurate reporting checks context and missing information; D Share the most surprising photo first.
questionSetB.evidence: Good reporting means asking what the image leaves out and giving readers enough evidence to think beyond the first impression.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: よい記事とは写真に写っていないことも考え、読者が第一印象を越えて判断できる根拠を示すものだと思います。
questionSetB.reason: 写真を文脈に合わせて扱うという結論。
